{{Short description|Soviet mathematician (1937–1993)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''Boris Gershevich Moishezon''' ({{langx|ru|Борис Гершевич Мойшезон}}) (October 26, 1937 – August 25, 1993) was a Soviet mathematician. He left the [[Soviet Union]] in 1972 for [[Tel Aviv]], and in 1977 moved to [[Columbia University]], where he was a professor of mathematics until his death sixteen years later.  He was a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] in 1983.

A resident of [[Leonia, New Jersey]], Moishezon died at [[Holy Name Medical Center|Holy Name Hospital]] in [[Teaneck, New Jersey]] on August 25, 1993, due to a [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]] he suffered while jogging.<ref>{{cite journal | title = Boris G. Moishezon, Columbia Professor Of Math, Dies at 55 | journal = [[The New York Times]] | date = August 27, 1993 | last1 = Saxon | first1 = Wolfgang | url = https://www.nytimes.com/1993/08/27/obituaries/boris-g-moishezon-columbia-professor-of-math-dies-at-55.html | access-date = August 24, 2011 | quote = Boris G. Moishezon, a mathematics professor at Columbia University who defected from the Soviet Union in 1972 and came to the United States five years later, died Wednesday. He was 55 and lived in Leonia, N.J. Dr. Moishezon had a heart attack while jogging and was pronounced dead in Holy Name Hospital in Teaneck, N.J., said his wife, Natalia.}}</ref>
